unseen_paired_holdout.interpretation: The independent holdout does not confirm a mean improvement. It supports a seed-dependent tail-regularization hypothesis: H5 repairs difficult trajectories while slightly harming easier ones.

rejected_screens.name: fixed_h10
rejected_screens.reason: smaller L4 gain and clean-regime worst regression

rejected_screens.name: speed_or_local_pd_adaptive_hold
rejected_screens.reason: local signals did not reproduce the h5 gain and harmed the hardest seed

rejected_screens.name: geometry_improvement_event_trigger
rejected_screens.reason: four-seed L4 worst improved only 0.0066 and one seed regressed by about 0.03

rejected_screens.name: gain_scheduled_movement
rejected_screens.reason: hard-seed mean improved but worst minimum fell from 0.6250 to 0.5909

rejected_screens.name: certificate_adaptive_h20_h5
rejected_screens.reason: calibration worst reached only 0.829 and worst minimum fell from 0.6250 to 0.5909; the lagged certificate was not a reliable reassignment trigger

rejected_screens.name: fixed_h3
rejected_screens.reason: calibration worst reached only 0.822 and worst minimum fell to 0.5789, disproving a monotone faster-is-better effect

decision: Retain H5 as an L4-specific tail-risk comparator, not a universal replacement. The unseen holdout rejects a general mean-gain claim but motivates a preregistered lower-tail objective on a new untouched bank.
